Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back. It has gone a bit cloudy, and the wind has picked up, which should aid the Dutch seamers. Babette de Leede has gathered her troops in a huddle before they take the field. Hasini Perera and Vishmi Gunarathne are the two Lankan openers. Iris Zwilling will open the attack for the Netherlands. Vishmi is on strike. Let's go...
... The Run Chase ...

Sri Lanka’s bowlers keep things tight - With the ball, Sri Lanka didn’t do much wrong and maintained control for most of the innings. The Lankans were particularly effective in the middle overs, drying up boundaries and forcing the Dutch to take risks. Sri Lanka will back themselves to chase this down. Stay tuned as the chase is coming up shortly...

Netherlands leave runs out there - Heather continued to strike the ball cleanly and looked the most dangerous batter in the park, but she spent too much time stranded off strike during the middle overs. That phase without boundary-hitting hurt the Dutch, as Sri Lanka’s bowlers tightened the screws and forced dot balls. Both Heather Siegers and Kalis missed out on half-centuries by a narrow margin.

Kalis stabilises the innings - The momentum wobbled when Phebe fell, but Sterre Kalis walked in and steadied the ship alongside Heather. The pair stitched together a calm, well-judged partnership that kept the scoreboard ticking without taking unnecessary risks. Their stand was the backbone of the Dutch innings, bridging the gap between the explosive start and the death overs. Both batters needed a few more boundaries in the middle phase to push the total into the 150s.

Dutch post 143 - The way the Netherlands Women started, they promised much more than just 143. After opting to bat first, the tone was set immediately by the openers, with Heather Siegers coming out swinging, and Sri Lanka’s bowling attack was put under instant pressure. Heather Siegers found the boundary at will in the Powerplay and looked in full control from ball one. Phebe Molkenboer struggled for timing at the other end, but Heather’s aggression ensured the Dutch still powered to 47/0 in the first 6 overs.

Commentary.Commentary: It is bright and sunny, and we are all set to get underway. A delayed start by around half an hour, but the good news is that no overs have been lost. Blue skies greet the two umpires as they walk out to the middle. Heather Siegers and Phebe Molkenboer are the two Dutch openers. Malki Madara will steam in first up for Sri Lanka. Siegers will face the first ball. Let's go...

PITCH REPORT - Shachi Pai is pitchside, and she says that it is really breezy out in the middle. Pai adds that it is a bit on the rougher side at one end and green on the other. Shachi feels that the bounce will be less than the previous game, and the umpires also looked a bit worried about a few wet patches. Believes that the ball will keep low and the keeper might need to stand a few steps ahead.

The stand-in skipper of Sri Lanka Women - Harshitha Samarawickrama informs that Chamari Athapaththu has been rested for this game. Harshitha says that they are looking to play good cricket in this game as they did in the previous one against Pakistan. Adds that they would have bowled first only as the wicket looks good.

The captain of Netherlands Women - Babette de Leede says the wicket looks nice and flat and they will aim to put a big score on the board and then back their bowlers to defend it. She adds that the preparation leading into the tournament has been excellent, and with this being their final warm-up game, the side is eager to put the finishing touches on their preparations before the main event gets underway. Babette also mentions that the Netherlands will be using 13 players in this fixture as they look to finalise their XI for their tournament opener on Sunday.

Sri Lanka Women - Hasini Perera, Vishmi Gunarathne, Imesha Dulani, Kavisha Dilhari, Nilakshika Silva, Kaushini Nuthyangana (WK), Harshitha Samarawickrama (C), Chamari Athapaththu, Hansima Karunaratne, Chethana Vimukthi, Sugandika Kumari, Kawya Kavindi, Malki Madara, Mithali Ayodhya and Nimasha Meepage.

Netherlands Women - Babette de Leede (C/WK), Myrthe van den Raad, Sterre Kalis, Sanya Khurana, Rosalie Lawrence, Phebe Molkenboer, Frederique Overdijk, Heather Siegers, Iris Zwilling, Robine Rijke, Caroline de Lange, Hannah Landheer, Isabel Van Der Woning, Lara Leemhuis and Silver Siegers.

TOSS - Right, the sun is out, and it is time for the coin to go up. No Chamari Athapaththu for Sri Lanka today. Harshitha Samarawickrama is leading the Lankans in her absence. Netherlands have won the coin flip and opted to BAT first.

2.03 pm GMT - We are hearing that the start of play has been delayed due to a wet outfield. While we await the next update from Derby, there is cricket elsewhere to keep you occupied. Over in Loughborough, New Zealand have won the toss and opted to bowl first against South Africa, so you can switch tabs and follow the action there while we wait for play to get underway here.

We should have had the toss by now, but there has been no word from the stadium just yet. Given the weather around, it would not be a surprise if the start is delayed. We are awaiting an official update, which should not be too far away, so stick around.

Rain threat - Derby has already had its fair share of rain today, with the earlier warm-up fixture between Scotland and Pakistan seeing only 9 overs possible in the second innings before the weather intervened. According to the Met Office, there are showers forecast during the game hours, but let's hope they stay away and allow for an uninterrupted contest.

Tactical takeaways - Looking at recent outings, both sides have experienced contrasting fortunes in their initial preparation games. The Netherlands suffered a heavy 58-run defeat to Scotland in their opening warm-up fixture, whereas Sri Lanka clinical dismantled Pakistan by 9 wickets, showcasing their top-tier form. For Sri Lanka, a commanding victory would solidify their tactical blueprints and maintain their supreme confidence, whereas for the Netherlands, managing to push a major nation like Sri Lanka to its limits would provide a massive morale boost.

Sri Lanka's core promise - The Asian side enters the match riding a wave of formidable momentum, anchored by their legendary captain, Chamari Athapaththu. Backed by an exciting mix of explosive youth and seasoned experience, including the dynamic batters such as Vishmi Gunarathne and Harshitha Samarawickrama, and spin-bowling all-rounder Kavisha Dilhari, the Lankan side brings immense subcontinental flair and tactical balance. Heading into this fixture, the team will focus on perfecting their death-bowling combinations, providing crucial middle-order batting practice to their lower-middle order, and ensuring the squad remains injury-free before the competitive pressure of the World Cup begins.

Netherlands aim to tick crucial boxes - The Dutch, led by captain and wicketkeeper Babette de Leede, enter this match looking to bounce back and fine-tune their combinations. Featuring a core of prominent players like Sterre Kalis, Robine Rijke, Heather Siegers, and primary all-rounder Iris Zwilling, the Dutch outfit has shown flashes of brilliance but lacks consistency against top-tier full members. In this encounter, the team's primary objectives will be addressing their middle-order batting durability, evaluating their operational depth, and giving their primary bowling assets an extensive workout under testing match conditions.

The dress rehearsal - Welcome to the historic County Ground in Derby, where Match 9 of the ICC Women's T20 World Cup Warm-up Matches sees tournament debutants, the Netherlands, face off against an in-form Sri Lankan outfit. Scheduled just days before the official tournament begins, this critical fixture provides a pressure-tested platform for both coaching staffs to test their game plans.
